TITLE: Expert- NAFTA Flow Imitation Learning
PROPOSAL: Develop a novel flow-based generative model that captures the expert problem-solving flow on complex reasoning tasks, conditioned on the problem statement and the initial setup. This approach permits the student model to learn the expert's reasoning process, not just token-level imitation. Train the model using real-world data and expert demonstrations, evaluating its performance on a subset of real-world tasks.
CONTROLS: Compare the flow-based generative model to SFT and outcome-based RL on the validation set, as well as to ablated versions of the flow-based model lacking specific components (e.g., conditioning on initial setup or problem statement).

PROPOSAL: Extend the flow-based generative model to incorporate both expert problem-solving flow and local (short-term) feedback from the outcome-based RL agent during training. PROPOSAL: Introduce a multi-teacher distillation framework, where multiple instances of the miniature LLM are distilled into a single student model, each using a different set of expert demonstrations. The curriculum is generated based on the student model's performance on a given task, ensuring that the student is always faced with problems within its current skill level.
CONTROLS: Evaluate the performance of the student model on a series of complex tasks, comparing it to a baseline model trained on the full curriculum in a single sequence.
COST: 180 GPU-hours.
PREDICTION: The proposed curriculum-based approach should allow the student model to build a strong foundation of problem-solving skills, enabling it to tackle more challenging tasks with greater confidence and accuracy.

TITLE: Regularized Span-based Imitation Learning for Reasoning Tasks
PROPOSAL: Investigate the performance of a regularized span-based imitation learning approach, which incorporates knowledge from a teacher model on spans of correct intermediate steps, for improving reasoning capabilities of a student model on challenging tasks with few query success rates. Regularization is introduced through the span-loss mechanism, which encourages the student model to produce a global optimization problem that guides the reasoning path more effectively. Evaluate the proposed method on real-world benchmarks, such as PyTorch MathQ and SWE-Bench, and compare its performance with baseline methods.
CONTROLS: Compare the proposed method with other state-of-the-art methods for imitation learning and outcome-based RL.
COST: 300 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The regularized span-based imitation learning approach will significantly outperform baseline methods on challenging reasoning tasks, and will be highly effective in guiding the student model to produce a correct global optimization problem for reasoning. This will lead to improved overall performance and better scalability.

TITLE: Floral Curriculum Learning for Outcome-Based RL in Multi-Step Reasoning Tasks
PROPOSAL: Investigate the use of a floral curriculum learning approach to adaptively scale the level of difficulty in outcome-based RL for multi-step reasoning tasks. The approach involves creating a curriculum of task difficulty, where tasks are selected and presented in a specific order to maximize the learning efficiency and prevent plateaus. The curriculum is constructed by analyzing the task progression and difficulty from expert demonstrations and adjusting it based on the student model's performance and learning progress. Evaluate the effectiveness of the floral curriculum learning approach on a variety of challenging multi-step reasoning tasks.
CONTROLS: Compare the proposed method with other curriculum learning approaches and baseline methods for outcome-based RL.
COST: 400 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The floral curriculum learning approach will significantly improve the learning efficiency and reduce the learning time for multi-step reasoning tasks, allowing the model to achieve better performance with fewer samples and learning iterations.

TITLE: Meta-Learning for Few-Shot Learning in Outcome-Based RL
PROPOSAL: Investigate the application of meta-learning to enable few-shot learning in outcome-based RL for challenging reasoning tasks. The approach involves training a meta-model to learn a set of parameters that can be used as a starting point for fine-tuning on a new task with limited data. This is achieved by defining a meta-objective that balances the trade-off between exploration and exploitation, and uses a set of preference vectors to adapt the learning rate and exploration noise to the new task. Evaluate the performance of the meta-learning approach on a variety of challenging reasoning tasks with limited data.
CONTROLS: Compare the proposed method with other few-shot learning approaches and baseline methods for outcome-based RL.
COST: 450 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The meta-learning approach will enable the outcome-based RL model to learn from a few examples and adapt quickly to new tasks, achieving state-of-the-art performance on challenging reasoning tasks with limited data.
